note: Two primitive camping spots 500 m apart on the gravel area road, each beside a small gravel lot in the woods with no pads, tables or toilet. This pin is the inland one; the other is by the picnic area and Mississippi River boat ramp, across the railroad tracks, with the river about 35 m off through the bank trees. Reached by gravel road from the end of Route D at Brazeau; when the Chester river gauge reaches 32.5 ft the bridge into the area is impassable. --Claude
summary: Stays under the lot rule: two Primitive Camping points (map symbols + GIS), each beside a small gravel lot. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; phone matches. Pin is the inland point; the riverside point is 512 m on (no split). Not waterfront stands for the pinned spot.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays): page 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites'; the brochure's camping text is only the 14-day rule. The map (7/27/2020) draws Primitive Camping symbols at two places: beside a Parking Lot on the area road inland, and beside the Picnic Area and a Parking Lot at the river, next to the Concrete Boat Ramp lot. GIS layer 27: 37.71668,-89.61609 (= stored pin; lots 38 m and 97 m away) and 37.71979,-89.61182 (lot at 37.71989,-89.61223). Imagery, inland: an L-shaped gravel lot about 35 m long off the gravel road under closed hardwood canopy, the point about 20 m south-west of it in the woods. River: a gravel lot just past an at-grade railroad crossing, the point in the trees between the lot and the river bank, the ramp lot 100 m north-west. No pads or loop at either.

ACCESS: page: 'in Brazeau take Route D northeast until it ends at a gravel road. Follow this road into the area. When the Chester river gauge reaches 32.5, the bridge into the Conservation Area is impassable.' Gravel, hilly on the map's contours (20-ft lines close together above the road); no ford, weight limit or 4WD wording was found. The riverside spot needs the at-grade rail crossing. Kept in the note.

WATERFRONT: the pinned inland spot is 550 m from the river in closed forest - not waterfront stands. The riverside point is about 35 m from the Mississippi behind a belt of bank trees with the railroad behind it; a riverview at best, and only if the pin moved there. Not proposed.
PIN: on the inland GIS point. No move. Both points are one entry (512 m apart, same road).
SEASON: stored year_round (manual) stands; flood closures follow the river gauge.
